Definition: to jump for joy, i.e. exult
BiblicalUsage: To jump for joy, to exult — and the Bible saves it for the joy that has a reason. Hannah sings it when the barren woman bears seven and the bows of the mighty are broken. The psalms sing it when God is trusted, when enemies fall back, when the righteous are glad before Him. This is not a vague happiness; it is joy with its feet off the ground because God has acted.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe joy like this is the right answer to what God does, not an extra. Hannah's song and the psalms agree: when God lifts the poor and breaks the bow of the mighty, the heart does not sit still. I hold that exulting is worship with the body in it, and a church that never jumps for joy has not yet heard what Hannah heard.
